one_line: Gatehouse gates bug-report submission on reproducible differential evidence.
what_it_does: Agents inspect a target, write and run a reproduction against pinned bad and fixed builds, and only then receive a submit_report tool; humans review the replayable receipt.
leverage_rationale: The live WebMCP tool surface is the workflow state: submission is unavailable until the evidence passes the differential gate, a relationship that ordinary UI automation would not reproduce as reliably.
leverage_evidence: Transcript describes submit_report appearing only after five consistent failures on the reported build and passes on the reference build.
Frames show submit_report absent, differential testing, then submit_report appearing.
Receipt/replay and exact build hashes are presented in the Devpost evidence.
execution_rationale: The packet shows a coherent editor, differential test, activity, approval, receipt, and replay flow, though fine-grained logs and end-to-end transitions are only partly legible.
execution_evidence: Frame sheets show introduction editor, differential test, activity panel, and the submit_report state transition.
Devpost screenshot shows signed/shareable receipt, replay, samples, hashes, and logs.
impact_rationale: It addresses a concrete and growing maintainer problem: cheap AI-generated reports that are not reproduced, while preserving human judgment.
impact_evidence: Transcript identifies open-source maintainers and unverified bug-report queues as the audience/problem.
Receipt is designed to travel into existing issue workflows.
creativity_rationale: Making tool availability itself an earned permission based on executable evidence is a memorable, deeply pursued interaction model.
creativity_evidence: No submit tool until the reproduction earns it; editing evidence revokes it.
Human approval remains separate from agent-produced proof.
usability_note: Clear staged workflow and replayable artifact; some evidence text is small in the frame sheets.
standouts: Tool availability as a stateful acceptance gate
advance_reason: Exceptional WebMCP leverage with credible product evidence and a distinctive, useful gate.

one_line: MarkDown Stripper prepares and privacy-checks documents for agent handoff.
what_it_does: It imports documents, converts and cleans them, extracts references, scans for sensitive data locally, and requires approval before redaction reads or export.
leverage_rationale: Document state, privacy findings, versioned approvals, and controlled redaction/export form a structured stateful handoff that is materially safer than DOM automation.
leverage_evidence: About text lists bounded inspect, handoff, privacy scan, readiness, and ID-based redaction tools.
Frames show Inspect/Protect/Export and structured copyable output.
Approval invalidates when relevant document state changes.
execution_rationale: The packet shows a coherent local-first workflow and processed outputs, but no video and limited direct proof of OCR/privacy results cap execution.
execution_evidence: Frame sheets show task selection, document workflow, detailed output, and copy controls.
Devpost screenshot shows the three-stage product UI.
impact_rationale: It addresses a real privacy and document-handoff problem for people using AI with sensitive files.
impact_evidence: Description names formatting repair, references, OCR, and sensitive-data detection before sharing.
Human approval is required before anything is shared.
creativity_rationale: The local-first, approval-invalidating handoff is a fresh synthesis of document cleanup and agent safety, though the category is familiar.
creativity_evidence: Inspect-Protect-Export flow with local scans and version-specific approval.
Agent discovery without server or JSON setup.
usability_note: The staged workflow and visible copy/output controls appear approachable.
red_flags: No submitted video; visual evidence is packaging/gallery material.
standouts: Approval tied to exact document version
advance_reason: Strong practical use case and meaningful structured handoff leverage.

one_line: A11yMCP lets agents negotiate authorized live accessibility adaptations.
what_it_does: Sites declare supported adaptations; an agent requests permission, applies a scoped change, and verifies that a keyboard-only shopper can complete checkout.
leverage_rationale: Negotiated capabilities, per-tool permissions, scoped verification, and shared live DOM state are central to the concept and not comparable to blind automation.
leverage_evidence: About text reports before/after tab order, radiogroup keyboard behavior, and scoped verification.
Frames depict checklist/progress, live application state, and verification-oriented workflow.
Description states cross-origin default-deny and explicit tool exposure.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a coherent accessibility adaptation and verification flow with concrete before/after claims, although the video is absent.
execution_evidence: Description gives a concrete checkout scenario and unauthorized-write counts.
Frames show staged browser workflow and green completion indicators.
Devpost thumbnail shows the A11yMCP demo and verification framing.
impact_rationale: It targets a specific, meaningful accessibility failure where a real shopper is blocked now, not merely audited later.
impact_evidence: Keyboard-only shopper cannot reach size options before adaptation.
The stated flow completes checkout while limiting changes to a negotiated profile.
creativity_rationale: The website honestly refusing unsupported adaptations, then negotiating and verifying authorized changes, is novel and memorable.
creativity_evidence: Honest no rather than fake stylesheet adaptation.
Adaptation contract and per-tool cross-origin permissions.
usability_note: Concrete task-oriented adaptation and verification; broader site integration may be complex.
red_flags: No submitted video; evidence relies on gallery and description.
advance_reason: High impact and unusually strong WebMCP-specific interaction model.

one_line: CloudTopology CPQ models multi-cloud architecture cost, egress, latency, and compliance.
what_it_does: Users compose cloud architectures on a visual canvas, inspect costs and audits, and export quotes or Terraform with WebMCP agent control.
leverage_rationale: Structured tools help agents manipulate architecture state and request calculations/exports, but much of the visible outcome is already available through a conventional visual CPQ UI.
leverage_evidence: Devpost image shows WebMCP Active with eight tools.
Visible canvas includes connected providers, spend, savings, egress, latency, CPQ, and Terraform controls.
Description claims real-time egress and GDPR audits.
execution_rationale: The screenshot shows a coherent, feature-rich dashboard and architecture canvas, but no video and limited end-to-end execution evidence.
execution_evidence: Visible metrics include total spend, savings, egress bill, and p95 latency.
Templates, nodes, audits, save/load, quote, and Terraform controls are visible.
impact_rationale: Cloud engineering teams have a credible need to compare cost, latency, egress, and residency tradeoffs in one model.
impact_evidence: Project frames a specific multi-cloud architecture and FinOps/CPQ audience.
Visible product includes concrete cost and latency outputs.
creativity_rationale: Combining architecture diagrams, dynamic egress modeling, compliance audits, and CPQ is ambitious, though adjacent tools exist.
creativity_evidence: Multi-cloud visual CPQ with live egress/latency and Terraform output.
WebMCP agentic control is integrated into the architecture workflow.
usability_note: Rich dashboard but likely dense for new users.
red_flags: No video submitted; screenshot is a paused demo/packaging view.
standouts: CPQ and infrastructure export in one workspace
advance_reason: Credible business value and substantial product surface, with moderate WebMCP delta.

one_line: MapForge lets organizations build and navigate custom indoor maps.
what_it_does: Editors trace buildings, floors, rooms, entrances, nodes, and routes; users navigate the resulting facility maps with agent assistance.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP agent operation is claimed, but the visible editor and navigation outcomes are plausibly achievable with ordinary UI automation and no structured agent action is demonstrated.
leverage_evidence: Description claims AI-agent intervention through WebMCP.
Screenshot shows MapForge Editor with buildings, floors, nodes, edges, routes, and publish controls.
No frame sheet or active agent invocation is supplied.
execution_rationale: The editor and floor-plan concept are visible, but the packet lacks video and provides limited proof of publishing or navigation completion.
execution_evidence: Devpost image shows floor-plan map, rooms, route lines, and editor controls.
About text describes editor and normal-user navigation roles.
impact_rationale: Indoor wayfinding is a real problem for hotels, universities, amusement parks, and other large facilities.
impact_evidence: About text gives concrete lost-in-building scenario and organization-built maps.
Visible map includes floors, rooms, entrances, and routes.
creativity_rationale: Organization-authored indoor mapping is useful and ambitious, but the map/editor category is established and the agent interaction is thinly evidenced.
creativity_evidence: Custom organization-scale indoor maps with agent-assisted creation/navigation.
Floor-plan editor includes semantic nodes and routes.
usability_note: Editor structure is understandable; end-user navigation is not demonstrated.
red_flags: WebMCP behavior is asserted but not visibly demonstrated.
advance_reason: Promising product concept, but evidence and WebMCP delta are too thin for advancement.

one_line: CUF deterministically verifies agent authorization without letting the agent grade itself.
what_it_does: A human declares a tenant boundary; WebMCP tools run cases, collect evidence, and a deterministic kernel returns PASS, FAIL, or INCONCLUSIVE with a sealed artifact.
leverage_rationale: The structured browser tool surface and shared evidence make authorization verification observable and constrain agent authority; the agent orchestrates but cannot supply the verdict.
leverage_evidence: Frames explicitly show tools registered from production origin and invoked through WebMCP rather than direct JavaScript.
Frames show deterministic PASS/FAIL/INCONCLUSIVE boundary evaluation and human policy.
Description lists case, evidence, verdict, and seal tools.
execution_rationale: The packet shows a coherent policy declaration, test harness, evidence, deterministic verdict, and export flow, with strong visual support despite some NOT RUN states in early frames.
execution_evidence: Frames show expected boundary, simulated regression/outage, own-tenant versus cross-tenant cases, and verdict panels.
Devpost thumbnail visibly shows a FAIL kernel verdict for an unauthorized ALLOW.
impact_rationale: Authorization regressions are consequential, and separating test execution from verdict ownership is valuable to security and platform teams.
impact_evidence: Concrete Tenant A/Tenant B isolation scenario.
Missing evidence yields INCONCLUSIVE rather than false PASS.
creativity_rationale: The agent-orchestrates/CUF-decides separation is a crisp and memorable trust model pursued through the tool and evidence design.
creativity_evidence: Agent cannot grade its own test.
Deterministic kernel distinguishes PASS, FAIL, and INCONCLUSIVE and seals evidence.
usability_note: Clear verdict model, though the security harness is specialized.
red_flags: Some frames visibly show NOT RUN states, though later frames show outcomes.
advance_reason: Strong technical execution and highly relevant WebMCP trust boundary.

one_line: Recall Response Workbench finds exact affected orders and stages a human-reviewed recall response.
what_it_does: It traces a supplier lot across 8,420 synthetic orders, isolates 37 exact matches from 213 lookalikes, stages quarantines/intercepts/outreach, and requires visible confirmation.
leverage_rationale: Structured domain tools enforce exact-match preconditions, synchronized state, and safe staging more reliably than an agent scraping tables and clicking controls.
leverage_evidence: Description reports exact 37/8,420 result and explicit exclusion of 213 lookalikes.
Frames show guided cleanup, analysis review, staged review, activity timeline, and safeguard confirmation.
Final commit remains a visible normal-page control.
execution_rationale: The packet evidences a coherent recall workflow from trace to classification, staged actions, review, and confirmation, though it is a synthetic rehearsal.
execution_evidence: Frames show exact target, analysis review, staged review, and confirm safeguards/release response.
Description states zero simulated commits before confirmation and a rehearsal receipt.
impact_rationale: Product recalls have a high-consequence precision problem: finding affected items while protecting lookalikes and keeping an accountable review gate.
impact_evidence: 8,420-order trace with 37 exact matches and 8,383 protected non-targets.
Staged quarantines, intercepts, and outreach are reviewed before commit.
creativity_rationale: The exact-lot/near-match protection framing and staged operational response are an ambitious, memorable application of agentic workflow safety.
creativity_evidence: Exact-match versus confusable-lot exclusion is central to interaction.
One atomic tool set follows the recall lifecycle and rejects out-of-order actions.
usability_note: Guided review, activity history, and visible confirmation support safe operation.
red_flags: Synthetic rehearsal only; no real operational integration is claimed.
standouts: Precision recall triage at realistic scale
advance_reason: High-impact, well-evidenced workflow with strong structured-tool value.

one_line: Synapse is a 3D spatial knowledge graph for human-agent exploration and learning paths.
what_it_does: It indexes documents into semantically linked 3D nodes, lets agents navigate and edit the graph, finds conceptual bridges, and persists the workspace.
leverage_rationale: Structured tools can coordinate graph navigation, indexing, and CRUD over shared state, but the same broad operations could be driven through a conventional interface with friction.
leverage_evidence: About text lists spatial navigation, BFS learning paths, cluster analysis, document indexing, CRUD, and persistence through WebMCP.
Devpost screenshot visibly presents the 3D spatial graph product.
No video frame sheets submitted.
execution_rationale: The concept and 3D product surface are packaged, but absent video and limited observable workflow evidence cap claimed execution.
execution_evidence: Devpost page and gallery evidence show a 3D spatial knowledge-graph interface.
Description specifies multiple functional subsystems but does not demonstrate them end to end.
impact_rationale: Researchers, learners, and knowledge workers can plausibly benefit from spatial associations and agent-generated learning paths.
impact_evidence: Description names document indexing, conceptual bridges, cluster analysis, and learning paths.
The product targets a recognizable limitation of flat notes/lists.
creativity_rationale: A living 3D knowledge graph with agents co-navigating and synthesizing paths is a fresh interaction model pursued beyond a simple chatbot.
creativity_evidence: Spatial semantic layout and agent camera navigation.
Graph algorithms are exposed as learning and organization interactions.
usability_note: Spatial exploration is distinctive but may be cognitively dense; usability is not demonstrated.
red_flags: Many capabilities are claims rather than observed evidence.
advance_reason: Creative concept, but execution and WebMCP evidence are too thin.

one_line: Respira exposes safe, staged WordPress editing tools directly on the page.
what_it_does: An agent reads site context, stages duplicate edits, audits content, and finds catalog gaps; a human approves or rejects drafts and can roll back.
leverage_rationale: Shared page context plus staged, permissioned, reversible writes give an agent a safer and more precise site-editing surface than generic browser automation.
leverage_evidence: About text describes page-local tools, staged duplicate edits, approval/rejection, audit, and rollback.
Agent-only approve/reject operations are meaningful as tools on the shared page.
Frames show iterative agent-builder/site-preview workflow and output states.
execution_rationale: The product story is coherent and the frames show site-building and workflow progression, but there is no video and the production WordPress integration is not directly observed.
execution_evidence: Description specifies 319 tools, permissions, REST execution, preview links, and rollback.
Frames show generated site preview, iterative prompts, and workflow/detail views.
Devpost screenshot presents the product and staged-edit claims.
impact_rationale: WordPress owners need safe agent-assisted edits across page builders without risking unreviewed production changes.
impact_evidence: Specific audience and workflow: site edits from ChatGPT with same-page approval.
Rollback and preview links support accountable operations.
creativity_rationale: Making a WordPress site itself the agent tool surface, with duplicate staging and human approval, is a strong and ambitious integration model.
creativity_evidence: Works across page builders through an abilities bridge.
Agent-only approve/reject and tokenized preview links are thoughtfully designed.
usability_note: Approval and rollback are clear safeguards; WordPress login/integration setup adds friction.
red_flags: No submitted video; integration breadth is primarily claimed.
advance_reason: Strong practical product and meaningful shared-state WebMCP leverage.

one_line: VoiceGuard is a synthetic voice-operations cockpit where agents spot risk and humans retain control.
what_it_does: An agent inspects call state, audits guardrails, drafts operator guidance, or stages a pause request; human clicks are required to apply guidance or pause the call.
leverage_rationale: The agent reads structured live call context and stages bounded actions in the same visible cockpit, while consequential operations are deliberately absent or human-gated.
leverage_evidence: About text lists four narrow tools and explicitly excludes dialing, sending, speaking, transfer, hangup, and campaign controls.
Shared activity trace and visible draft/request state are central to supervision.
Devpost screenshot identifies native Chrome WebMCP inspector and audit_guardrails output.
execution_rationale: The scope is intentionally coherent and the cockpit/tool model is well specified, but no video means execution is claimed from packaging and description.
execution_evidence: Description specifies read-only tools, draft guidance, pause staging, and trusted human clicks.
Devpost page shows the synthetic cockpit/demo framing and WebMCP inspector claim.
impact_rationale: Consequential voice operations need human accountability and visible guardrail review; the synthetic demo addresses that supervisory need.
impact_evidence: Audience/problem is operators supervising voice AI calls.
Human approval gates guidance application and call pause; all data is clearly fictional.
creativity_rationale: A shared voice-operations cockpit with deliberately bounded agent authority is a strong safety-oriented synthesis, though the cockpit category is familiar.
creativity_evidence: No tool for the agent to directly speak, dial, transfer, or hang up.
Agent finds signals while human owns action in the same visible page.
usability_note: Narrow actions and visible trace support supervision; synthetic data limits real-world validation.
red_flags: Synthetic-only scenario and no submitted video.
Actual call-state execution is not independently visible.
advance_reason: Good safety design and credible WebMCP supervision use case, with moderate evidence limits.
